run.question: Database connection timeouts are occurring for blue-whale app in namespace app-94

report.summary: Investigation of the reported database connection timeouts for app blue-whale in namespace app-94 (runbook fetched and followed: database-troubleshooting). Findings: the blue-whale Deployment in app-94 (created 2026-11-22T08:44:52Z, 1/1 ready) points DB_HOST at postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local:5432; the Service postgres in app-94 exists (ClusterIP 10.96.93.52, port 5432, selector app=postgres-db) but its Endpoints object returned subsets: null, i.e. no backing addresses. Cluster-wide object inventories show app-94 contains exactly one pod (blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-9wbp2) and that no Postgres Deployment, StatefulSet or Pod exists in any namespace, so the postgres Service has nothing to route to. That pod is Running, ready, restart count 0, with only Normal startup events (Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started) and no Failed/BackOff/Unhealthy events. Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every query in this Run and the pod's container logs returned zero lines, so blue-whale's own error text, error rate and latency were not observable. Conclusion is partial: the dependency gap (no database backend behind the Service that DB_HOST targets) is directly observed and is the strongest explanation for failing or timing-out database connections, but the fault's occurrence at blue-whale and the exact failure mode are unverified, and the object that should supply the database is absent rather than visible. Runbook steps: (1) pods and events checked - pod running, only Normal startup events; (2) logs checked - no lines returned, connection errors not verifiable; (3) service and endpoints checked - postgres Service present, Endpoints empty; (4) in-pod nc connectivity test not carried out, no exec tool available; (5) database health (psql) not carried out, no postgres pod exists and no exec tool available; (6) connection-pool env checked in the Deployment spec (DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20).

claims.text: Deployment blue-whale in namespace app-94 was created 2026-11-22T08:44:52Z with 1 replica and sets container env DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20; image python:3.9-slim, app code mounted from secret blue-whale-app.

Service postgres in namespace app-94 is a ClusterIP Service with clusterIP 10.96.93.52, port 5432 -> targetPort 5432, and selector app=postgres-db; both app-94 Services (blue-whale and postgres) were created at 2026-11-22T08:44:52Z.

Endpoints object postgres in namespace app-94 has subsets: null (no addresses at all), while Endpoints blue-whale in the same namespace has an address 10.244.0.28 pointing at pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-9wbp2 on port 8080.

The full cluster pod inventory returned 33 pods; the only pod in namespace app-94 is blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-9wbp2 (phase Running, ready true, restartCount 0, startTime 2026-11-22T08:44:52Z), and no pod named postgres* appears in any namespace.

The cluster-wide Deployment inventory returned 25 deployments and contains no postgres deployment (only app-94/blue-whale plus kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo workloads); the only StatefulSet in the cluster is otel-demo/alertmanager.

Ownership chain confirmed: ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 (created 2026-11-22T08:44:52Z, readyReplicas 1) is owned by Deployment blue-whale, and its pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-9wbp2 is owned by that ReplicaSet.

All events involving app-94 objects in the window are Normal and describe only the fresh start: Pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-9wbp2 Scheduled (2026-11-22T08:44:52Z), Pulled, Created, Started (08:44:53), ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 SuccessfulCreate, and Deployment blue-whale ScalingReplicaSet 'Scaled up replica set blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 from 0 to 1'.
Namespace app-94 contains only one ConfigMap, kube-root-ca.crt; no database-related ConfigMap or fault-injection configuration object is present in app-94.

Two Warning events FailedToCreateEndpoint ('endpoints "postgres" already exists', 2026-11-21T08:28:31Z and 2026-11-21T09:05:28Z) and one for 'sqlserver' (2026-11-21T09:21:49Z) name the involved-object namespaces app-217 and app-223, which are not among the 8 currently existing namespaces (app-94, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo); they do not concern app-94.

The blue-whale pod shows no sign of its own failure: phase Running, ready true, restartCount 0, no lastState termination recorded, and no Failed, BackOff, Unhealthy or Killing events for app-94 in the window.

Most likely cause of the reported database connection timeouts: DB_HOST postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local resolves to Service postgres in app-94, whose selector app=postgres-db matches no pod and whose Endpoints object has no subsets, and no Postgres workload exists anywhere in the cluster, so every connection from blue-whale to 10.96.93.52:5432 has no reachable backend and fails or times out.

A client-side or configuration-side cause cannot be excluded: blue-whale's code lives in Secret blue-whale-app (not readable in this Run) and DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30 / DB_POOL_SIZE=20 are the only pool settings visible in the Deployment spec, so whether the app reports timeouts for a reason other than the empty postgres endpoints is unverified.

Rejected: blue-whale's pod itself crashed, restarted or was evicted and that produced the errors. The pod is Running and ready with restartCount 0, no lastState termination reason is recorded, and no Failed/BackOff/Unhealthy events exist for app-94 in the window.

Rejected as a cause of this incident: otel-demo's fault-injection component flagd being switched on for blue-whale. flagd is deployed only in namespace otel-demo, app-94 contains nothing but the blue-whale Deployment and the kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap, and no evidence ties an otel-demo fault setting to blue-whale or to the app-94 postgres Service.

Restore a database backend for the app-94 postgres Service (deploy the intended Postgres workload in app-94 with label app=postgres-db, or repoint DB_HOST/DB_PORT of Deployment blue-whale at the real database), then confirm Endpoints postgres gains addresses and re-read blue-whale logs for connection successes.

Advisory follow-up: read Secret blue-whale-app out-of-band to review /app/app.py connection handling, and enable or attach the client-side error signal (pod logs or metrics) so the timeout error text and error rate can be confirmed rather than inferred.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for every query in this Run (get_metric_names, get_label_values, execute_prometheus_instant_query 'up', and metrics_range_query kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="app-94"} all returned status error / SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error-rate, connection or latency series for blue-whale or postgres exists in this evidence; those values are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unreachable for every query in this Run (traces_list_services and traces_search for service frontend returned status error / SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no span-level evidence of blue-whale or of failed database calls was available.

The blue-whale container log read for pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-9wbp2 returned status no_data with zero lines (lines_read 0, no previous container instance), so the exact timeout/error text and whether failures are occurring right now were not observed; the absence of log lines is unknown, not proof of no errors.
Further log reads of the same pod also returned status no_data with zero lines, so no application-level connection error could be read.

The application code and any credentials are stored in Secret blue-whale-app, which cannot be read in this Run; the client-side connection logic and the value actually used for DB_HOST at runtime could not be verified.
Queries for NetworkPolicies, ResourceQuotas and PersistentVolumeClaims each returned no objects (status no_data), so a blocking policy, quota or storage shortfall is unchecked rather than excluded.

A statefulset query filtered to postgres returned status no_data with zero matching objects, so the absence of a Postgres StatefulSet is a query that matched nothing rather than a certified inventory fact.

No Postgres Deployment, StatefulSet, Pod or PVC exists now; whether such a workload ever existed in app-94, who removed it and when are unknown, and the change_history integration is not available in this Run.
Whether the app-94 postgres Service selector (app=postgres-db) matches the labeling the DB workload is supposed to carry cannot be verified because no such workload is present.

In-pod connectivity testing (nc) and database health checks (psql) from the database-troubleshooting runbook could not be carried out: no exec capability is available, and there is no postgres pod to connect to.
next_steps: Check the deployment source/manifests for app-94 to see whether a Postgres workload (Deployment or StatefulSet labeled app=postgres-db) was supposed to be created alongside Service postgres, and restore it if so.
If the database is intentionally external, update Deployment blue-whale's DB_HOST/DB_PORT to the real endpoint and roll the deployment.
After the backend exists, run kubectl exec from the blue-whale pod (e.g. nc -zv postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local 5432) and re-read blue-whale logs to confirm connections succeed.
Restore Prometheus and Jaeger reachability for this target so blue-whale's error rate, latency and traces can be checked against a baseline.
